Rules / Modernization

SK1028 Decode a byte span without an array copy

Encoding.UTF8.GetString can consume an existing byte span without a temporary ToArray allocation.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 7.2
Since1.3

Why

Span<byte> and ReadOnlySpan<byte> already describe the contiguous bytes to decode. Calling their ToArray solely for GetString copies the bytes and allocates an intermediate array. The replacement is offered only when speculative binding selects the framework's span overload, preserving the existing span/slice computation.

Example

Instead of:

string Decode(System.ReadOnlySpan<byte> bytes) => System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetString(bytes.Slice(1).ToArray());

Write:

string Decode(System.ReadOnlySpan<byte> bytes) => System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetString(bytes.Slice(1));

When it does not fire

Only the framework Encoding.UTF8 property, GetString(byte[]) and instance Span<byte>/ReadOnlySpan<byte>.ToArray are recognized. Arbitrary Encoding implementations, LINQ ToArray, named arguments, array range rewrites and expression trees are excluded; array/null/bounds semantics are not guessed. Existing offset/count overloads are not reported. Requires an available span overload. Concurrent mutation of the input buffer is not made safe by either form; callers must synchronize it.
